text:
1. **LMRL Gym: Benchmarks for Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning with Language Models** — The closest exact match: eight multi-turn dialogue/text-game environments, with LLMs acting as simulators for training and evaluation. People: Marwa Abdulhai, Isadora White, Charlie Snell, Charles Sun, Joey Hong, Yuexiang Zhai, Kelvin Xu, Sergey Levine. Affiliations: UC Berkeley and Google DeepMind.  
   URL: [lmrl-gym.github.io](https://lmrl-gym.github.io/)

2. **Consistently Simulating Human Personas with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning** — Trains simulated patients, students, and social-chat partners using multi-turn RL; introduces benchmarks for persona consistency and reports more than 55% less inconsistency. People: Marwa Abdulhai, Ryan Cheng, Donovan Clay, Tim Althoff, Sergey Levine, Natasha Jaques. Affiliations: UC Berkeley, University of Washington, and Google DeepMind.  
   URL: [arXiv:2511.00222](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.00222)

3. **MUA-RL: Multi-turn User-interacting Agent Reinforcement Learning for Agentic Tool Use** — Places LLM-simulated users directly inside the RL loop and evaluates on TAU2 Retail/Airline/Telecom, BFCL-V3 Multi Turn, and ACEBench Agent. People: Weikang Zhao, Xili Wang, Chengdi Ma, Lingbin Kong, Zhaohua Yang, Mingxiang Tuo, Xiaowei Shi, Yitao Zhai, Xunliang Cai. Listed affiliations: Meituan, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Peking University.  
   URL: [arXiv:2508.18669](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.18669)

4. **UserRL: Training Interactive User-Centric Agent via Reinforcement Learning** — A unified multi-turn RL framework built around standardized gym environments and simulated users; studies turn-level credit assignment, trajectory scoring, and simulator choice. People: Cheng Qian, Zuxin Liu, Akshara Prabhakar, Jielin Qiu, Zhiwei Liu, Haolin Chen, Shirley Kokane, Heng Ji, Weiran Yao, Shelby Heinecke, Silvio Savarese, Caiming Xiong, Huan Wang. Affiliations: Salesforce AI Research and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.  
   URL: [arXiv:2509.19736](https://arxiv.org/abs/2509.19736)

5. **SimulatorArena: Are User Simulators Reliable Proxies for Multi-Turn Evaluation of AI Assistants?** — The most relevant simulator-validation benchmark: 909 human–LLM conversations in math tutoring and document creation, used to measure how well simulated users reproduce human behavior and rankings. People: Yao Dou, Michel Galley, Baolin Peng, Chris Kedzie, Weixin Cai, Alan Ritter, Chris Quirk, Wei Xu, Jianfeng Gao. Affiliations: Georgia Institute of Technology and Microsoft.  
   URL: [ACL Anthology](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1786/)
